subject: Media Literacy
title: Reader Bias and Selective Exposure
description: A 60-second lesson on Reader Bias and Selective Exposure.

hook.text: You follow news accounts that confirm your views and unfollow those that challenge them. Everyone does.

buildup.text: Selective exposure is our tendency to seek information that confirms existing beliefs and avoid contradictions.

discovery.text: Research shows people spend 36% more time reading articles that align with their pre-existing opinions.

twist.text: Media bias starts with you. Before blaming outlets, ask what you're choosing to consume and why.

climax.text: The media you consume is a mirror of your biases as much as a window to the world.

punchline.text: You blame media bias. But you chose the media.

quiz.question: What is selective exposure?
options: Seeking information that confirms your beliefs and avoiding contradictions
Being exposed to too much media
